title: Fixed matching Fourier bound
statement: Let $r,k,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n>0$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ whose nonzero Fourier coefficients are all indexed by sets of cardinality $k$, and let $M$ be a perfect matching in the complete $2r$-partite graph with $k$ vertices per part. Assign independently and uniformly a label from $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to each edge of $M$. For each part, take the absolute value of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by the set of labels on its incident matching edges. The expected product of these factors is at most $\left(\frac{k!}{n^k}W_k(f)\right)^r$, where $W_k(f)$ is the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients indexed by $k$-element subsets of $[n]$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube

$M$ is a perfect matching in the complete $2r$-partite graph with $k$ vertices per part
